```{python}
import pandas as pd
from pyprojroot import here
import plotly.express as px
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

```{python}
cms_race = pd.read_csv(here("projects/hayden_project/datasets_files/cms_race.csv"))

school_locations = pd.read_csv(here("projects/hayden_project/datasets_files/cms_school_locations.csv"))

school_coords = school_locations[['agency_code', 'latitude', 'longitude']].copy()

cms_race["agency_code"] = cms_race["agency_code"].astype(str)
school_coords["agency_code"] = school_coords["agency_code"].astype(str)

cms_map_info = cms_race.merge(school_coords, on = 'agency_code', how = 'left')

meck_all = pd.read_csv(here("projects/hayden_project/datasets_files/meck_all.csv"))

```

```{python}
fig = px.scatter_map(
    cms_map_info,
    lat = 'latitude',
    lon = 'longitude',
    color = 'pct_black',
    hover_name = 'name',
    hover_data = {
        'pct_black': ':.1f',
        'sts_per1000': ':.1f',
        'iss_per1000': ':.1f',
        'rpt_per1000': ':.1f',
        'arr_per1000': ':.1f',
        'latitude': False,
        'longitude': False},
    color_continuous_scale = 'Viridis',
    center = {'lat': 35.26, 'lon': -80.84},
    zoom = 8,
    title = 'Racial Composition of Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools')

fig.show()
```

I think that this map does a great job of visualizing the the racial organization of students throughout Mecklenburg County. While I don't think this is a finalized visualization in its self, I do think it's a good jumping off point for adding/altering. I'm considering adding a different layer that looks at school funding. I am struggling slightly with narrowing down my focus. Part of me feels that my project doesn't relate strongly enough to the criminal legal system. I need to put a bigger emphasis on the disciplinary rates, law enforcement referrals, and school-related arrests. I'm thinking that my second visualization could have a bigger focus on this. 

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 9))

# ISS vs. referrals
ax[0, 0].scatter(
    np.log1p(meck_all["iss_per1000"]),
    np.log1p(meck_all["rpt_per1000"]),
    alpha=0.5)
ax[0, 0].set_title("ISS vs. Law Enforcement Referrals")
ax[0, 0].set_xlabel("Log(1 + ISS rate)")
ax[0, 0].set_ylabel("Log(1 + referral rate)")

# STS vs. referrals
ax[0, 1].scatter(
    np.log1p(meck_all["sts_per1000"]),
    np.log1p(meck_all["rpt_per1000"]),
    alpha=0.5)
ax[0, 1].set_title("STS vs. Law Enforcement Referrals")
ax[0, 1].set_xlabel("Log(1 + STS rate)")
ax[0, 1].set_ylabel("Log(1 + referral rate)")

# ISS vs. arrests
ax[1, 0].scatter(
    np.log1p(meck_all["iss_per1000"]),
    np.log1p(meck_all["arr_per1000"]),
    alpha=0.5)
ax[1, 0].set_title("ISS vs. School-Related Arrests")
ax[1, 0].set_xlabel("Log(1 + ISS rate)")
ax[1, 0].set_ylabel("Log(1 + arrest rate)")

# STS vs. arrests
ax[1, 1].scatter(
    np.log1p(meck_all["sts_per1000"]),
    np.log1p(meck_all["arr_per1000"]),
    alpha=0.5)
ax[1, 1].set_title("STS vs. School-Related Arrests")
ax[1, 1].set_xlabel("Log(1 + STS rate)")
ax[1, 1].set_ylabel("Log(1 + arrest rate)")

plt.suptitle("School Discipline and Law Enforcement Contact Across Mecklenburg County")

plt.show()
```

I think this visualization is also a good start thought the issue that I'm running into is the fact that a lot of schools have 0 law enforcement referrals and school-related arrests. This is why there's a long stream of dots at the bototm of each plot. I'm not sure if it would be representative or right to remove these values or if I should keep them. 

Together I think these two visualizations could be good and I also think it could be really good if I incorporated school funding, racial demographics of Mecklenburg County as a whole, and maybe socioeconomic status of schools. Idk I need to fine tune and narrow down.
